newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to visit Poland, Romania after NATO summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to visit Poland, Romania after NATO summit.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has decided to visit Poland and Romania after nexth month's NATO summit in Madrid, White House officials said on Thursday.
Senior administration officials said Clinton wanted to visit one of the three countries that the United States has backed for NATO membership at the July 8-9 summit.
Clinton has said he favours admitting the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary into NATO in the first of what he hopes will be a series of enlargements.
France and several other NATO members favour a larger expansion and want Romania or Slovenia, or both, admitted now as well.

Officials said Clinton also wanted to visit one of the countries that was in the running for NATO membership, but which has not been backed by Washington, to show that the United States was open to their membership at a later date.

Clinton is scheduled to leave the United States for Europe on July 5, shortly after after America's July 4 Independence Day. He will attend the 16-nation NATO summit, then travel to Bucharest, Romania and Warsaw, Poland.
He will wind up his European trip with a state visit in Denmark. Clinton had been due to visit Copenhagen earlier this year, but the trip was postponed because of his knee injury.

A senior administration official said the president's idea in visiting Poland was to welcome the country as a new member of NATO, while at the same time reminding it and the other new members of their obligations as members of the alliance.
His purpose in visiting Romania was to reassure people there that their country was an excellent candidate for NATO membership in the next round of expansion.
Clinton is due to return to the United States July 12.
